commonPrompt:
Create production-quality 2D cartoon character artwork of FURO, using the single attached reference as the definitive identity and drawing-style reference. This is a cohesive set of isolated character action illustrations for a cozy pet game. Preserve the reference character: oversized round head, pale dusty cherry-pink short bob, black horizontal side hair clips and black geometric bang clips in the same arrangement, cream-white face, large rose-red eyes, pink blush, tiny w-shaped mouth, extremely small soft white animal-like body, two stubby white forepaws with NO human fingers and two dark chocolate-brown rear feet. Keep the head-to-body proportions and face anatomy of the reference; this is a tiny mascot, not a human girl. No animal ears, no tail, no Doro flower, no Mint cat ornament, no new identity accessories. Clothing/accessories only when the individual action explicitly requests them.
Match the smooth warm 2D cartoon illustration style of the reference: confident dark-brown outlines, rounded silhouettes, soft cel shading with a restrained gentle gradient, moderate material detail, small soft highlights, upper-left lighting. Clean finished art, not pixel art, not 3D, not a sketch, no grain or paper texture, no excessive glossy highlights. Use a pure white #FFFFFF background with no floor shadow, no horizon and no surrounding room. Objects and the complete character must stay fully inside each cell with clear white margins and an empty white gutter between cells. No text, letters, numbers, speech bubbles, grid lines, panel borders, labels, signature or watermark. Never draw ZZZ, HMM or LEVEL UP. Only draw effects specifically mentioned in the action.
All poses use the same front-facing or very slight three-quarter view, consistent head size, line weight and visual scale. Preserve expressions and individual action silhouettes without redesigning the character. Each cell is a separate finished illustration. Read cell descriptions in row-major order. In paired reusable-action frames, keep all parts in exactly the same positions except the stated facial or tiny pose changes. Empty prop slots must really be empty; do not fill them with placeholder blocks, outlines or demonstration food. The paws are visible rounded side brackets around that reserved area. This is a raw artwork sheet for human review; do not add diagrams or exploded layer illustrations.
